Adrastus.what: Adrastus stops the fight at his gate, recognizes the oracle and feasts Polynices and Tydeus.
Adrastus pledges his daughters Argia and Deipyle to Polynices and Tydeus.
Adrastus sends the seers to read omens and counsels patience; Argia pleads with him.
Adrastus questions the guide, learns she is Hypsipyle, and calms the crowd after Lycurgus' attack.
Adrastus presides over the games and shoots the arrow foretelling he alone will return.
Adrastus fails to part the brothers and flees the duel.

Tydeus.what: Tydeus arrives at Argos and fights Polynices at Adrastus' door.
Tydeus demands the throne from Eteocles, then kills fifty ambushers, sparing only Maeon.
Tydeus returns wounded and inflames the Argives for war.
Tydeus defeats the giant Agylleus in wrestling.
Tydeus rampages, is mortally wounded by Melanippus, and gnaws his head.
Tydeus' corpse is fought over and mourned by Polynices.

Capaneus.what: Capaneus scorns prophecy and the seers' warnings, and the crowd cheers him.
Capaneus helps kill the serpent that killed Archemorus.
Capaneus boxes Alcidamas, is wounded and dragged away enraged.
Capaneus helps Hypseus kill Hippomedon on the riverbank.
Capaneus scales Thebes' wall, defies the gods and is struck by Jove's thunderbolt.

Polynices.what: Polynices is exiled, travels through a storm to Argos and fights Tydeus at the gate.
Polynices weds Argia and grows homesick for Thebes.
Polynices is thrown from his chariot in the race.
Polynices collapses in grief and tries to kill himself over Tydeus' body.
Polynices, driven by the Fury, duels Eteocles and both die.
Argia and Antigone find and burn Polynices' body.

Amphiaraus.what: Amphiaraus reads dire omens on Mount Aphesas and foretells his doom to the crowd.
Amphiaraus declares the events fated and calls for funeral honours for Archemorus.
Amphiaraus wins the chariot race with Apollo's help.
Amphiaraus slaughters foes until the earth swallows him alive.
Amphiaraus arrives alive in the underworld and terrifies Dis, who spares him.

Eteocles.what: Eteocles is goaded by Laius' phantom, refuses Tydeus and sends the ambush.
Eteocles frets over the ambush and faces Maeon's defiance.
Eteocles gathers allies and orders his troops against the Argives.
Eteocles, taunted by Creon, bursts out to fight and kills Polynices while dying.

Jove.what: Jove resolves to punish Thebes and Argos, swears by the Styx, and sends Mercury.
Jupiter sends Mars to rouse Argos and warns the gods not to interfere.
Jupiter sends Mercury to Mars and tells Bacchus Thebes will not fall now.
Jove strikes Capaneus with a thunderbolt.
Jove turns his gaze from the brothers' coming crime.

Oedipus.what: Blind Oedipus prays to Tisiphone to set his sons against each other.
Oedipus joins the Theban banquet, secretly delighted at his sons' war.
Oedipus mourns his dead sons and is exiled to Cithaeron by Creon.

Tisiphone.what: Tisiphone answers Oedipus and sows hatred between the brothers.
Tisiphone inflames the war and maddens Bacchus' tigers.
Dis orders Tisiphone to create a new horror.
Tisiphone, disguised as Halys, lures Hippomedon from Tydeus' corpse.
Tisiphone calls Megaera and drives the brothers to fight, repelling Piety.

Juno.what: Juno pleads for Argos in Jove's council.
Juno pleads with Jove to save Hippomedon.
Juno sends Iris to Sleep to bind the Thebans.
Juno leads the Argive women and lights the plain for Argia.

Hippomedon.what: Hippomedon hurls a stone at the serpent that killed Archemorus.
Hippomedon wins the discus with a mighty throw.
Hippomedon slaughters Thebans in the Ismenos and kills Crenaeus.
Hippomedon is overwhelmed by the flooded river and killed by Hypseus and Capaneus.

Menoeceus.what: Menoeceus accepts death and kills himself on the wall to save Thebes.
Menoeceus is honoured above all the Theban dead.

Argia.what: Argia marries Polynices and wears the cursed necklace.
Argia begs Adrastus to grant war for Polynices.
Argia finds Polynices' body and burns it with Antigone.

Jocasta.what: Jocasta goes to the Argive camp and begs Polynices for peace.
Jocasta pleads with her sons, then stabs herself.

Antigone.what: Antigone surveys the Theban leaders with Phorbas from the tower.
Antigone pleads with her brothers and guides Oedipus.
Antigone burns Polynices' body with Argia and is seized by guards.

Bacchus.what: Bacchus dries up the rivers to delay the Argives.
Bacchus guides Hypsipyle to save Thoas.
Bacchus begs Jupiter to spare Thebes.

Creon.what: Creon urges the watch-fires around the Argive camp and loses his son Menoeceus.
Creon taunts Eteocles to fight, then seizes the throne and exiles Oedipus.
Creon forbids burial of the Argives and is killed by Theseus.

Diana.what: Diana answers Parthenopaeus' prayer in the footrace rerun.
Diana arms Parthenopaeus and tries to save him before Mars drives her off.

Laius.what: Mercury leads Laius' ghost up; disguised as Tiresias he goads Eteocles.
Laius' ghost prophesies Theban victory and a curse on Oedipus' sons.

Parthenopaeus.what: Parthenopaeus leads the Arcadians; his mother Atalanta begs him to stay.
Parthenopaeus wins the footrace after being cheated by Idas.
Parthenopaeus kills many with arrows, then is mortally wounded by Dryas.

Apollo.what: Apollo sends a phantom so Amphiaraus wins the chariot race.
Apollo aids Amphiaraus, then leaves him to the earth.
Apollo tells Diana fate cannot be changed.

Amphion.what: Amphion's patrol catches and kills Hopleus and Dymas.

Archemorus.what: Archemorus is killed by a serpent while Hypsipyle tells her tale.

Atalanta.what: Atalanta runs from the woods and begs Parthenopaeus to stay home.
Atalanta has terrible dreams and prays to Diana.

Venus.what: Venus pleads for Thebes before Jupiter.
Venus, neglected, drives the Lemnian women to murder their husbands.
Venus rouses Mars to drive Diana off.

Mars.what: Mars, compelled by the Fates, drives through Greece spreading war-fever.
Mars obeys Mercury and sends Panic to stir the Argives.
Mars forces Diana away from Parthenopaeus.

Hypsipyle.what: Hypsipyle guides the thirsty Argive army to Langia's stream.
Hypsipyle tells her story, saves Thoas, and loses Archemorus to the serpent.
Hypsipyle is reunited with her twin sons.
Eurydice blames Hypsipyle and demands her death.

Ismene.what: Ismene tells her dream and sees dying Atys, her betrothed.

Mercury.what: Mercury guides Laius' shade up from the underworld to Thebes.
Mercury rouses Mars in Thrace at Jupiter's command.

Tiresias.what: Tiresias and Manto raise the ghosts of the dead.
Tiresias reads omens and demands the last of the serpent's brood.

Agylleus.what: Agylleus is thrown by Tydeus in wrestling.

Bellona.what: Bellona hurls her spear and arms the Argive camp.

Eurydice.what: Eurydice laments her son and demands Hypsipyle's death.

Hopleus.what: Hopleus seeks Tydeus' body and dies with Dymas.

Hypseus.what: Hypseus fights Hippomedon and kills him on the bank.

Lycurgus.what: Lycurgus tries to kill Hypsipyle in his rage.
Lycurgus burns his sceptre and hair at his son's pyre.

Maeon.what: Maeon returns alone, curses Eteocles and kills himself.

Manto.what: Manto assists Tiresias in raising the dead and describes the ghosts.

Palaemon.what: Palaemon reports the chasm that swallowed Amphiaraus.

Pallas.what: Pallas aids Tydeus, then flees in disgust when he gnaws Melanippus' head.

Phegeus.what: Phegeus carries Theseus' challenge to Creon.

Thiodamas.what: Thiodamas is chosen augur and prays to Earth and Amphiaraus.
Thiodamas calls for and leads the night raid on Thebes.

Thoas.what: Thoas is saved by Hypsipyle from the Lemnian slaughter.

Agenor.what: Agenor dies trying to save his brother in the slaughter at the Ismenos.

Alcidamas.what: Alcidamas boxes Capaneus and wounds him with skill.

Aletes.what: Aletes consoles the mourners, recalls Thebes' earlier woes and curses Eteocles.

Melampus.what: Melampus goes with Amphiaraus to Mount Aphesas and reads the omen of birds killing each other.

Arion.what: Arion bolts in the chariot race and throws Polynices.

Melanippus.what: Melanippus wounds Tydeus, who gnaws his head; Melanippus is killed.

Atys.what: Atys is killed by Tydeus, then is carried dying to Ismene and sees her.

Coroebus.what: Coroebus slays the monster killing Argive infants and offers himself to Apollo.

Crenaeus.what: Crenaeus, the river's grandson, is killed by Hippomedon and mourned by his mother.

Dis.what: Dis rages at the living seer and orders Tisiphone to make a new horror.

Dymas.what: Dymas helps find Tydeus' body and dies with Hopleus when Amphion's patrol catches them.

Eriphyle.what: Eriphyle takes Harmonia's necklace from Argia, bribed with gold, sending Amphiaraus to war.

Evadne.what: Evadne, Capaneus' wife, begs Theseus to compel burial of the Argive dead.

Gorge.what: Gorge kills her husband Elymus on the night of slaughter.

Idas.what: Idas cheats Parthenopaeus in the footrace by seizing his hair.

Ide.what: Ide mourns her twin sons slain in the ambush.

Iris.what: Iris carries Juno's command to Sleep in his cave.

Ismenis.what: Ismenis laments her son Crenaeus, killed by Hippomedon.

Ismenos.what: Ismenos complains to Jove over his grandson's death and floods against Hippomedon.

Jason.what: Jason arrives at Lemnos with the Argonauts, fathers twin sons with Hypsipyle and leaves.

Megaera.what: Megaera is summoned by Tisiphone and drives Eteocles against his brother.

Minerva.what: Minerva counsels Tydeus during the ambush and receives his vow of a temple.

Ornytus.what: Wounded Ornytus warns the Argive women of Creon's decree, and Argia resolves to go on alone.

Panic.what: Panic, sent by Mars, stirs the Argives at Nemea and they rush to arms.

Phorbas.what: Phorbas names the Theban leaders to Antigone from the tower and tells tales of them.

Piety.what: Piety halts the armies briefly until Tisiphone drives her away.

Polyxo.what: Polyxo rouses the abandoned Lemnian women to murder their husbands and swear a bloody oath.

Sleep.what: Sleep, commanded by Juno through Iris, leaves his cave and lulls the Theban watch.

Theseus.what: Theseus, begged by the widows, marches on Thebes, routs the Thebans and kills Creon.

Virtue.what: Virtue, disguised as Manto, inspires Menoeceus to accept death for Thebes.
